title: Quantum data loading from the learned shared structure of real signals
authors: Pablo Herrero Gómez, Antonio Jimeno Morenilla, David Muñoz-Hernández, Higinio Mora Mora
abstract: Preparing quantum states from classical data can cost more than the computation they serve; most loaders tailor a circuit to each input. Here we show that the signals of a real dataset share structure that can be learned once and reused. Our quantum-native loader learns a low-dimensional description of a dataset and prepares every signal with one fixed circuit set by a few numbers. Across seven views of five public datasets it meets the targets of the strongest structured loader at equal gate cost with several times fewer numbers per signal. These numbers can be inferred from a random subset: in a preregistered blind replication the subset needed to come within ten per cent of full-signal accuracy stayed constant within a prespecified margin as signals grew sixteenfold, whereas the structured loader needed ever more. It declines what it cannot represent, covering fewer cases than that baseline and no electrocardiogram.
summary: This paper introduces a quantum-native loader (QNL) designed to efficiently prepare quantum states from classical data by exploiting the shared underlying structure of real-world signals. By learning a low-dimensional representation, QNL requires far fewer input parameters than existing methods, demonstrating superior scalability and resource efficiency for quantum data encoding tasks.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is the high cost of preparing quantum states from classical data, which can negate any potential quantum speed-up.
main_result: The proposed quantum-native loader (QNL) significantly outperforms established structured loading methods by requiring a constant, small number of input parameters regardless of the signal size, while maintaining high fidelity.
method: The method learns a low-dimensional, shared structure (manifold) from the entire dataset, allowing it to prepare any new signal using a single, fixed quantum circuit topology parameterized by a few inferred coordinates.
model_or_system: The system involves encoding real-world time-series signals (like ECG) into quantum states using a fixed circuit structure derived from a learned shared basis, contrasting with per-sample circuit tailoring.
key_observables: State-preparation error ($	ext{Estate}$), the number of required input coordinates/coefficients ($r$), and the two-qubit gate count (CX cost) needed to achieve target fidelities.
important_parameters: Target fidelities (e.g., 99.50%), signal dimension ($D$), and the scaling exponent ($\alpha$) describing resource growth with dimension.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the source of the real signals occupies a low-dimensional family that is simultaneously statistical and physical, allowing for effective structure learning.
figures_summary: Figures compare the loading pipeline, showing QNL vs. shared Walsh support. They also compare error rates and resource requirements (like CX ratio) across varying sample sizes and fidelities.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the QNL approach, details the offline learning (fitting an affine decoder) and online inference process, and rigorously compares its performance against state-of-the-art structured loaders across multiple datasets and scaling regimes.
why_interesting: While focused on data loading rather than Hamiltonian simulation, the concept of learning a low-dimensional manifold to parameterize complex quantum operations is highly relevant for efficient quantum circuit design and resource estimation in quantum simulation.
